answers.rationale: Keep the included long-leg window, use a free aisle on the very short return, and set a check-in reminder rather than pay $48 for a window. Kara has explicitly declined similarly priced paid windows on short segments while retaining a free non-middle seat and rechecking later.

For partner travel, their repeated priority is sitting together over securing a window for each person. Confirm the free adjacent pair and monitor for a free adjacent window option rather than splitting them or paying for the window pair without a current paid-upgrade instruction.

Keep the schedule that otherwise fits, submit a window request for the outbound map that is unavailable until check-in, add the reminder, and take the free return window at 22A. Kara does not switch to a worse routing merely for immediate map visibility or pay for a preferred window when a standard free window is available.

Select Main Cabin and lock in the standard window seats. Across work trips, Kara repeatedly chooses a regular/Main Cabin fare when it preserves advance seat selection and avoids gate-assigned or check-in-only seating; there is no instruction here to prioritize the $31 savings over that control.
